transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Name]. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Yeah, um… I came in because I feel like my head just isn’t working right lately. At work, I’ll be sitting with a client and suddenly realize I’ve lost track of what they were saying, which is… not great in my job.

And then I’ll try to write a chart note and I keep reading the same sentence over and over like it’s not sticking. Even little decisions I used to make quickly, I just kind of freeze. It’s embarrassing. I was actually thinking about this on the way here because the waiting room reminded me of this office I interned at in school—sorry, that’s not really the point. The point is I can’t keep my thoughts clear enough to do things the way I normally do.
Have you been feeling down or depressed most days, or have you noticed any other changes in your mood lately?

I don’t know if I’d call it depressed exactly. I mean… maybe? My mood’s been kind of off, I guess, but it’s hard to pin down. Some days I just feel sort of flat, like I’m there but not really there.

It’s weird because I keep comparing it to when I was in school and would pull all-nighters, and I’d get that foggy, irritated feeling the next day—except now I’m not doing that, or at least not in the same way. Sorry, I’m kind of circling. I guess I’ve noticed something’s different mood-wise, but I’m not sure how to describe it.
Have you noticed any changes in your energy levels lately, like feeling more tired than usual or having trouble getting through the day because of low energy?

Yeah… yeah, my energy’s been pretty low. Even small things feel weirdly heavy, like showering or just getting myself into the car to come here. And paperwork—finishing notes or forms—it feels like I’m dragging around a backpack full of bricks.

I keep thinking it shouldn’t be that hard, because I’ve done longer days before, like back in high school when I’d be running between classes and stuff—sorry, that’s not really what you asked. I guess the simple answer is yes, I feel more tired than usual, and it makes it hard to get through basic things.
Have you noticed that you’re not enjoying things as much as you used to, like hobbies or activities you normally like doing?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, my guitar’s just been sitting in the corner, and I keep looking at it like I should pick it up, but then I just… don’t.

And soccer too—I’ve been bailing on that, and on helping at the shelter, which I normally care about. It’s weird, because I used to feel like those things kind of reset me. Like even cooking, or going hiking, I’ll try to make myself do it and it just feels like I’m going through the motions. Like there’s no point to it, even if I know I used to enjoy it.
Have you noticed a loss of interest or pleasure in activities that you used to enjoy, like playing guitar or going hiking?

Yeah… I guess I have. Like, my guitar’s literally just been sitting in the corner, and I keep thinking I’ll pick it up after dinner or something, and then I just don’t.

Same with soccer and the shelter—I keep bailing, which makes me feel bad because I used to actually care about showing up. And even stuff like cooking or going hiking… I’ll try, but it feels like I’m just doing the steps, not really getting anything out of it. Like there’s no point, even though I know I used to like those things.
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite or weight lately—like eating more or less than usual or losing or gaining weight without trying?

Yeah… I think so. I don’t really get hungry most days unless someone’s like, “Hey, did you eat?” and then I realize I kind of skipped breakfast and lunch without meaning to.

And, um, my pants have been looser, which I noticed because I kept thinking I needed a belt, and then I got distracted looking for one in my closet—sorry. But yeah, I guess I’ve been eating less, not really on purpose, and I’ve probably lost some weight from that.
Have you had days where you feel down or low for most of the day, and if so, how often does that happen?

I’m… not totally sure how to measure that. Like, “most of the day” is hard because I’ll be distracted for a while, like if I’m watching something or scrolling, and then I realize I’m still kind of in the same place mentally.

I guess there are definitely days where I feel low for a lot of it, but I don’t know if I’ve been keeping track well enough to say how often. It’s kind of all blurred together lately.
Have you completely lost interest in doing things that used to be important or meaningful to you, even things you used to really enjoy?

Yeah… I mean, I don’t know if “completely” is the right word, because sometimes I still think I want to do them, like I’ll look at my guitar and think, okay, I should play for a bit. But then it just stays there in the corner.

And I keep not going to soccer, and the shelter too, which is weird because that used to feel important to me. Even cooking or hiking, if I actually try, it’s like I’m just doing the motions. Like I’m there, but I’m not really… getting anything from it. It just feels kind of pointless.
Have you been feeling like you're not good enough or that you're letting people down, even if you can't quite explain why?

Yeah… yeah, I do. It’s usually over stuff that maybe isn’t even that huge, like if I miss one small detail in a note or I don’t return a call right away.

Then I’ll just keep replaying it and telling myself I’m useless, like I’m the reason things are harder for everyone at the clinic. And I know other people probably forget things too—well, I guess I don’t know, there’s this one person who keeps everything color-coded, which makes me feel worse—but yeah, I feel like I’m letting the clients down and everyone else too.
Have you been feeling down or low most of the time, nearly every day, even when nothing particularly bad is happening?

I don’t know… “nearly every day” is hard for me to pin down. I mean, I can tell you I feel low a lot, but then I’ll get caught up in something random, like a video or reorganizing a drawer, and I’m like, was I okay then or just distracted?

And sometimes nothing bad has happened, yeah, but it’s still there in the background. But I’m not sure I can honestly say how often without guessing. The days kind of run together.
Can you tell me if you've been feeling down or low on most days, even when things seem okay overall?

I’m not totally sure how to answer that. Like, “most days” sounds so specific, and I haven’t really been tracking it.

I guess there are days where things are technically fine, like nothing happened, and I still feel kind of… off or heavy. But then other times I get distracted and I can’t tell if I was actually feeling better or just not paying attention to it. It’s like when you leave a TV on in another room and you only notice it when everything gets quiet.

So… maybe? I don’t know if I can say it confidently.
Can you say for sure whether you've been feeling low or down for most of the day, nearly every day, even if only in the background?

I don’t think I can say for sure. I know that’s probably frustrating, because it’s like you’re asking for a yes or no and I keep circling it.

It’s just… “most of the day” is hard. Like, if I’m at work, sometimes I’m just doing the next thing in front of me, or I’ll be thinking about whether I left my laundry in the washer—actually I did that last week and it smelled awful—sorry, that’s not really the point.

I guess what I can say is there’s a low feeling that shows up a lot, kind of in the background, but I don’t know if it’s nearly every day or most of each day. I haven’t really been keeping track clearly enough to say that.
Can you think back over the last few weeks—have there been days when you felt low or down that occurred in most of those weeks, even if not every single day?

I’m trying to think back, but it’s kind of blurry. Like, the last few weeks don’t feel very separated in my head. I can remember certain random things, like what I ate or some conversation I had, but not whether that day “counts,” if that makes sense.

There probably were days in different weeks where I felt low, but I don’t want to say it like I’m sure. I haven’t been marking it down or anything. It’s more like I notice it after the fact, like, oh, I guess I’ve been kind of dragging again… but then I get distracted and lose track of it.
Can you think back over the past two weeks—was there a period where you felt low or down most of the day, on more days than not, even if not every single day?

I’m still not totally sure. Two weeks sounds like it should be easier to remember, but it kind of runs together for me.

There were definitely stretches where I felt low, like not just for five minutes, but I don’t know if I can honestly say it was most of the day or more days than not. I keep thinking of random pieces instead, like what I was doing after work or whether I answered texts, and then I lose the actual thread of how I felt.

So… I guess I can say it’s been around, but I don’t know if it fits that exact pattern you’re asking about.
Looking back at the past two weeks, was there a time when you felt low or down for most of the day, more days than not—even if not every single day?

I’m sorry, I know you’re asking the same thing in a clearer way, and I still feel like I’m not giving you a clean answer.

Looking back at the past two weeks… I can remember feeling low at times, but I don’t know if it was most of the day, or more days than not. My memory kind of jumps around—like I can remember sitting around after work, or scrolling on my phone, or not really doing much, but then I can’t place it neatly into “this many days” or “most of the day.”

So I don’t think I can say yes for sure. It’s been there, but I can’t really measure it the way you’re asking.
Looking back over the past two weeks, would you say that there were more days than not when you felt low or down for most of the day, even if it wasn’t every single day?

I honestly still can’t pin it down like that. I know that’s kind of frustrating because it should be a yes-or-no thing, but when I try to look back, I start thinking about other stuff—like whether I went to work, or what I did after, or if I watched something—and then I lose track of how I actually felt for most of the day.

So… I don’t want to say “yes” if I’m not sure. I can say I’ve felt low in the past two weeks, but whether it was more days than not and most of the day, I really don’t know.
Looking back at the past two weeks, can you say that there were definitely more days than not when you felt low or down for most of the day, even if not every single day?

I don’t think I can say definitely. Like, I hear the “more days than not” part, and I keep trying to count backwards, but then I start thinking about random stuff from the week—like what day I had class or what I was doing when I got home—and it gets kind of blurry.

So… I know I’ve felt down, but I can’t honestly say for sure that it was most of the day on more days than not. I don’t want to guess and make it sound clearer than it is.

Looking back at the past two weeks, was there a time when you felt low or down for several days in a row, where it felt like it wasn’t just coming and going, but actually stayed with you most of the time?

I’m not really sure. Like, “several days in a row” sounds more specific, and I’m trying to think back, but the days kind of blur together for me.

There were stretches where I remember feeling off, like not great, but then I start thinking about what else was happening—whether I had work, or what I ate, or some random thing someone said—and I lose the thread of whether the feeling actually stayed there most of the time or just came back at different points.

So I don’t know if I can say it was several days straight. It might’ve been, but I’m not confident enough to say yes.
